title: Best Insurance Lead Vendors: 7 Picks by Coverage and Lead Type
summary: Compare seven insurance lead vendors for auto, home, commercial, group health, Medicare and final expense. Know which lead type to test and what to track.
body_markdown:
Start with the coverage you write and the way your team answers. For auto and home web leads, put EverQuote first on your demo list and compare it with QuoteWizard. For staffed inbound calls, start with SmartFinancial. Tivly, NextGen Leads, Benepath and Lead Heroes are first calls for small commercial, Medicare, group health and final expense, respectively.


*Trellus publishes this guide and sells a dialer for insurance teams. We picked vendors based on the coverage, delivery formats, targeting and sharing terms they documented on November 19, 2026. The picks reflect fit for each workflow. Compare results with your own pilot before you commit to volume.*


## Best insurance lead vendors by use case


Where to start, what each vendor says it delivers, and what to confirm before buying. Buying need Vendor Documented offer Check before ordering


Auto and home web leads, first pick[EverQuote](https://go.everquote.com/pro/faq) Exclusive and shared lead options. The FAQ says shared leads can go to up to three agents, with one agent per carrier. Confirm the distribution limit and filters for your exact product and territory.


Auto and home web leads, second pick[QuoteWizard](https://agents.quotewizard.com/insurance-leads/) Quote forms from its own and partner sites, delivered by email or an eligible CRM. Its[buying guide](https://agents.quotewizard.com/resources/5-things-to-know-when-buying-insurance-leads/) describes a four-agent maximum for shared leads. Ask which sites supply your campaign and whether the original source reaches your CRM.


Live phone transfers[SmartFinancial](https://agents.smartfinancial.com/) Marketplace data leads and live transfers it describes as screened and sent to one agent. Ask what makes a transfer billable and what happens if your team misses it.


Small commercial[Tivly](https://tivly.com/commercial-insurance-leads) Commercial lead campaigns with industry, geography and business-size preferences. Ask for sample inquiries in two industries you actually write and confirm the delivery format.


Medicare[NextGen Leads](https://www.nextgenleads.com/leads/medicare-insurance-leads) Medicare call and data lead products. Its[campaign documentation](https://docs.nextgenleads.com/support/campaign-settings) describes product-specific filters and a forwarding number for calls. Ask which product is available for your market and have your compliance lead review a sample inquiry and its permitted follow-up.


Group health[Benepath](https://www.benepath.net/leads-faq/) Advertises exclusive real-time leads, inbound calls and aged records for group health and other lines. Confirm exclusivity in the written order. The[published terms](https://www.benepath.net/terms-and-conditions/) default to non-exclusive unless the order specifies otherwise.


Final expense callbacks[Lead Heroes](https://leadheroes.com/final-expense-life-leads/) Markets exclusive callback leads generated through conversations and says it reviews recordings for lead quality. Ask for a sample of the original request, the delivery schedule for your territory and the replacement terms for the package.


## Choose fresh web leads, live transfers or aged leads


### Fresh web quote requests


A buyer submits a quote form and the vendor sends the contact information to your agency. Shared distribution makes the follow-up schedule important because several agents may receive a request close together. When comparing EverQuote and QuoteWizard, keep the same coverage line, territory and staffing hours. Ask each vendor to show a sample lead as it arrives, including the original inquiry time and what the shopper requested.


### Live transfers


The vendor hands a current call to your team. The agency needs someone qualified and free to answer during delivery hours. Ask how the vendor screens the call, what information the person answering receives, and whether a short, abandoned or misrouted call can be credited. Track missed transfers separately so they remain visible when you compare vendors.


### Aged insurance leads


An aged lead is a past inquiry. Ask for the original submission date and the age at delivery. For group health, Benepath has an[aged lead program](https://www.benepath.net/aged-leads-2/) you can compare with its real-time offering. Ask whether the same inquiry has already been assigned, what source and permission records come with it, and which replacements are available. Use a separate pilot for aged leads so that their results remain comparable.


## Run a small lead vendor pilot


1. **Match coverage and territory.** Pick one coverage line, a geography you serve and one delivery type. Compare two vendors where possible. Ask each vendor for a sample record, the original form or call context, sharing terms, contact permissions and credits in writing.
2. **Check how records arrive.** Use a test record to check the CRM fields for vendor, campaign, timestamp and lead format. Your team should be able to find the request and see any restrictions before following up. Ask who handles suppression or opt-out changes after delivery.
3. **Match the follow-up.** Use the same delivery window and team procedure for comparable batches. Record when the lead arrived and when the first attempt started. Log duplicate contacts, wrong numbers, out-of-territory records and missed transfers separately.
4. **Score the outcome.** Count unique leads delivered, leads reached, quotes sent, policies issued and credits received. Use the same follow-up window for each vendor and keep the denominators visible.


Copy these columns into a spreadsheet for each vendor and order:` vendor, coverage, territory, lead format, delivered, duplicates, reached, quoted, issued, lead spend, credits, agent hours` . Compare contact rate as unique leads reached divided by unique leads delivered. Calculate cost per issued policy as net lead spend after credits divided by policies issued, and review agent hours separately. When no policy has issued, keep the spend and mark that rate pending.


A sample of ten leads that reaches three people and produces two quotes still needs time for those quotes to become issued policies. Keep web leads, live calls and aged records in separate rows. Their delivery and staffing costs differ.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is the best insurance lead company for independent agents?


Start with the line you plan to grow. For fresh auto and home quote requests, compare EverQuote and QuoteWizard on the same territory and schedule. For small commercial inquiries, include Tivly and ask how it filters by business type and size. Your pilot should show which vendor sends leads your agents can quote.


### Are exclusive insurance leads worth buying?


Ask what exclusivity means in the written order. It may apply to a single distribution channel or a specific delivery event. A shopper could also submit a quote request to another site. Compare net cost per issued policy against a shared batch with the same coverage line, territory and follow-up window.


### How do you compare aged leads with new quote requests?


Use a separate batch for each format and record the time of the original inquiry. Run the same outcome definitions for contact, quote and policy issued. Consider the extra follow-up time on each batch and ask your agency’s compliance team to review what contact channels and follow-up are appropriate.


Once you pick a lead source, decide how agents will work the list and record the outcome. The[Trellus insurance dialer workflow](https://www.trellus.ai/solutions/insurance) shows how quote follow-up can start from contacts your team already manages in a supported CRM.
